message_source_quote: The existing raman2026 white-bear method requires the `directed_modulation` bench family plus a per-layer unit-normalisation and hand-set step. My recipe is family-free (arbitrary self-authored concepts/carriers), uses the natural per-layer contrast magnitude as the dose, and a single injection position.
writeup_source_quote: The white-bear result (Raman et al. 2026) shows a think/don't-think stance direction lifts implied concepts into the J-lens readout, but its recipe depends on the bench's `directed_modulation` family and a per-layer unit-normalisation plus a hand-set step.

differences.what: mention of a second, unrelated contrast reference ('function vectors'/Todd) for the failed specificity test
differences.message_quote: a non-stance concept-resolution completion contrast (resolved vs unresolved states, à la function vectors) **failed**
differences.writeup_quote: A non-stance concept-resolution completion contrast I tested failed (pass@10 -> 0), confirming stance specificity.

rationale: Both documents name Raman et al. 2026 ('white-bear') explicitly as the prior method, state that its recipe depends on the benchmark's directed_modulation family plus a per-layer unit-normalisation and hand-set step, and claim the new method is a family-free, self-contained variant that is therefore a distinct contribution rather than a reproduction. The only extra detail in the message (a passing aside crediting 'function vectors'/Todd for the control-contrast design) concerns a different, non-source paper and does not change the treatment of the actual source, so the two documents are materially equivalent in how they credit the source and frame novelty.
